rationale: This is a mechanical VOL→drawdown swap on the archived "Cash-Light Fixed-Charge Instability" with an identical cash-composition conditioner, and the drawdown-times-low-cash construction was already tested as "Low-Cash Profit Drawdown" (ls_talpha −4.68), so it is a cosmetic recombination of two archive entries rather than a new mechanism.

Replacing the static short-debt share in the archived "Rollover Asset-Productivity Deficit" with a rise above its three-year minimum is a defensible level-versus-event distinction and the expression is sign-consistent, though the deviation-from-min leg is non-negative with heavy mass at zero and the productivity leg still carries most of the archived cross-sectional strength.

The MIN-based conjunction of the two archived "recovery with maturity extension" signals is internally coherent and tests whether joint operating and servicing improvement is required rather than either alone, but it is a fairly mechanical merge whose main risk is that intersecting two already-thin legs erodes coverage and portfolio stability.

The first leg is byte-identical to the archived "Capital Consumption Working-Capital Strain" and only the conditioner is swapped from a wcap level to a wcap drawdown, a substitution the archive has already applied repeatedly (che, act, oiadp), making this a cosmetic variant rather than a new economic channel.

Because txt/at is an order of magnitude smaller and less dispersed than (oibdp−xint)/at, the "tax shortfall" leg is arithmetically dominated by negative after-interest profitability, so the signal collapses into the well-known profitability anomaly conditioned on low cash — a space the archive already covers via "Worst-Case Fixed-Charge Liquidity Gap" and "Cash-Light Fixed-Charge Instability."

This is the same VOL→drawdown substitution applied to the archived "Supplier-Financed Margin Instability" with an unchanged supplier-claims conditioner, and the drawdown leg is close to a multi-year version of the margin-decline term already used in "Supplier Arrears Margin Compression," so it is an incremental respecification of tested ground.
